To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existing operating systems for IoT are not able to meet all the needs of IoT applications and that there is a need for a generic operating systems framework that can be used to design an operating system that is tailored for IoT devices.
the existing operating systems for IoT are not yet ready for the real world.

the IoT operating systems are designed for the purpose of providing a common platform to the IoT devices, and are characterized by a high degree of heterogeneity in terms of hardware, software and network.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (i) to present the state-of-the-art in operating systems for IoT (ii) to identify the essential features of an OS tailored for an IoT device (iii) to propose a generic framework that captures these features (iv) to identify the gaps in the existing OSs and (v) to provide a roadmap for the future research.
the design of an IoT OS that is lightweight, scalable and energy efficient.
the development of an OS for IoT devices, which is a critical step towards the realization of the IoT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single OS that can be used to address all the requirements of IoT.
IoT operating systems are still evolving and there is no single best solution that can meet the demands of all the applications.
IoT operating systems are still in the nascent stage of evolution, and the future of IoT devices lies in the hands of researchers who are able to design an efficient operating system for IoT devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while there is a lot of scope for research in this domain, the existing operating systems for IoT are far from perfect and there is still a long way to go.
the current operating systems for IoT are not mature enough to be used in real world.
the existing operating systems are inadequate to cater to the needs of IoT devices, and that there is a need to develop new operating systems for the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of an operating system for IoT devices is not an easy task.
a new breed of OS for IoT devices is required to address the issues of heterogeneity, security, energy efficiency, and real-time constraints.
there is no single operating system that is able to satisfy the diverse demands of all the applications of IoT.
